name: LeverUp USD
oneLiner: lvUSD is LeverUp's Monad liquidity-layer stablecoin minted against USDC; MON backs the separate LVMON token.
collateral: USDC collateral supporting LeverUp's liquidity-layer stablecoin (lvUSD) for perpetuals and margin trading; MON collateral backs the separate LVMON token.
pegMechanism: Synthetic stablecoin used inside LeverUp's Monad liquidity layer, with mint, burn, and redemption mechanics tied to the protocol's collateral and trading engine

mechanismArchetypeReview.rationale: Monad transaction 0x6752e0a90a52ad24ba2037d9e3b38e5050cf4d7ba45a4b384177fce2fc64b7cb created the exact tracked lvUSD contract at block 31,946,424 on October 28, 2025. LeverUp's documentation describes automatic USDC-backed minting with protocol-managed TWAP, auction, and redemption controls, supporting the existing algorithmic archetype.

oracleRisk.summary: LeverUp describes lvUSD as a USDC-backed liquidity-layer token stabilized through protocol-internal TWAP anchoring, LV auctions, and redemption quotas rather than an external liquidation oracle.

branchApplicability.reviewer: Codex Safety Score V9 oracle review
branchApplicability.rationale: LeverUp documents lvUSD as an automatically minted liquidity-layer asset backed by USDC positions, with TWAP-based price anchoring and protocol auctions/redemptions when the token trades below its target. The reviewed product description does not expose borrower-owned collateral positions, per-market collateral thresholds, or a token-level liquidation branch, so the V9 collateral-liquidation inventory does not apply.

blacklistabilityReview.evidence: 2026-07-30 on-chain re-review of the sole tracked Monad deployment 0xfd44b35139ae53fff7d8f2a9869c503d987f00d1 at block 91734906. Token is a non-proxy contract (EIP-1967 implementation/admin slots zero; runtime code ~4170 bytes). Resolved selectors include blackList(address) public mapping, updateBlackList(address,bool) (reverts "only operator" for non-operators), setOperator(address) (Ownable: only owner), transfer/transferFrom, mint, burn/burnFrom, owner, and issuer — no separate pause() selector. At observation: owner()=issuer()=VMMV engine 0x135951057cfccca7e8ef87ee41318d670f723f68 (itself owned by 3/5 Safe 0xf9bd99a8e5be72adf687b304ed0e0234e0ebccba per mintAuthority), operator()=0x0 so no active blacklister is appointed, and blackList(sample addresses)=false. eth_call transfer from Safe succeeds for a non-blacklisted holder, so ordinary transfers are unrestricted until an operator sets blackList. Owner can appoint an operator and thereby enable holder freezes; that is a direct token-level blacklist surface (reviewedStatus true). Failure domain: LeverUp owner/operator path on Monad. Upstream Circle USDC collateral freeze remains a separate inherited reserve exposure and is not the lvUSD token control path.

reserveReview.rationale: LeverUp documents lvUSD as the liquidity-layer token automatically minted when a trader opens a position with USDC collateral and redeemable through the protocol's USDC reserve flow. MON collateral mints the separate LVMON token and is not part of lvUSD's direct dependency set.
reserveReview.compositionBasis: Current LeverUp documentation for collateral-specific liquidity-layer issuance
reserveReview.knownUnknownExposure: No additional direct lvUSD collateral asset is identified in the current issuance documentation; protocol trading gains or losses can change reserve coverage but do not introduce another authored reserve dependency.

custodyProfile.reviewer: Kimi P2 reserve cohort rc-6 (lead usx-solstice)
custodyProfile.uncertainty: lvUSD's USDC collateral sits inside LeverUp's protocol trading system on Monad rather than with a named legal custodian; the reviewed documentation does not establish account segregation, insolvency treatment, or collateral reuse terms, and trading gains or losses can change reserve coverage.

notices.title: Perpetuals liquidity-layer stablecoin
notices.message: lvUSD is included through CoinGecko price and market-cap coverage, but its collateral and redemption model are tied to LeverUp's trading system rather than a conventional issuer reserve.

mintAuthority.summary: lvUSD is minted inside LeverUp's VMMV trading engine on Monad when traders open lvUSD positions against USDC collateral; mint is gated by 'only issuer' resolving to a 3/5 GnosisSafe (0xf9bd99...) with no modules. Token is not upgradeable.

controls.label: LeverUp VMMV trading-engine (minter)
controls.capDescription: lvUSD is auto-minted by the LeverUp trading engine when a trader opens a position using USDC collateral, so minting is economically bounded by collateral inflow; the engine contract itself cannot raise that bound. MON collateral mints the separate LVMON token, not lvUSD.
controls.evidence: 2026-07-20 on-chain: lvUSD 0xfd44b35139ae53fff7d8f2a9869c503d987f00d1 issuer() = owner() = this contract (170-byte EIP-1967 proxy, implementation 0x1d4bcd07f4779e25b4d2f58dfaf91614b932e7ba), whose owner() = the 3/5 Safe 0xf9bd99a8e5be72adf687b304ed0e0234e0ebccba. LeverUp docs state the system automatically mints lvUSD when a trader opens a position with USDC collateral; MON collateral backs the separate LVMON token.

controls.label: LeverUp protocol admin multisig
controls.evidence: Monad block 80607552: lvUSD owner() = 0x135951... (EIP-1967 proxy), impl = 0x1d4bcd..., whose owner chain leads to 0xf9bd99... — a GnosisSafe proxy (masterCopy slot 0 = 0x29fcb43b46531bca003ddc8fcb67ffe91900c762, Solidity 0.7.6 singleton). getOwners() returned 5 addresses; getThreshold = 3; getModulesPaginated returned 0 modules.

review.evidence: Monad block 80607552: lvUSD mint reverts with 'only issuer'; issuer() = owner() = 0x135951... (proxy chain terminating at a 3/5 GnosisSafe 0xf9bd99...). Safe has 3-of-5 threshold, 5 owners, 0 modules. Token not upgradeable (EIP-1967 admin slot = 0). Confirmed: concentrated EOA/Safe-controlled issuer with no modules or bypass.
